assign.request: UX rethink pass 2 on /imagine/blogx/ - the reviewer-brief.md in ux-rethink, realm=blogx
steps: build + measure an alternative (cards: real stills, per known pattern)

log.msg: FIVE SENTENCES (before). what: a lab comparing eight complete blog-front layouts against the same eight fake posts. use: click any of eight cards on the landing wall, then click a post or the floor strip to compare. goal: leave knowing which of the eight shapes to actually build a real blog on. hard: 3/5 - the prose is clear but the landing wall's eight cards carried only an icon and one line each, so the reader could not tell a hero-plus-wall front from a rail-driven archive without opening every one, on a page whose whole subject is what the layout looks like. better: swap the eight icon cards for real screenshots of each shell.

ALTERNATIVE, per the disproof memo: this landing page is already a wall of 8 same-shaped children, and the approved-five tile wall is exactly the shape it uses - the 3-column card is already disproved for that shape, not spending tokens re-proving it. Checked the other two options honestly instead. Approved five: already correct (tile wall). Paging vocabulary surface change: the click from the wall into a shell, and from a shell into a post, is not launch/expand/swap/takeover - Blog.container() skips the columns row's own $pages and mounts straight into app.$pages, so a shell is not a column at any width word, it physically relocates out of the /imagine/ row entirely (more drastic than takeover, which only hides ancestors' layout without unmounting them). This is a deliberate, already-documented choice (blogx.css/readme: two rails - the site's and the blog's own - would read as two navigations), it touches all 8 shells plus Section/Post/Part, and it buys nothing measurable (the visual result already IS a full-screen takeover) - re-wiring it is the CLAUDE.md major-surgery case (a dozen callers), so it is left for the owner to say whether blogx should adopt the formal width:"full" word for consistency's sake, not silently changed.

BUILT AND MEASURED: Blog.js gets a preview(nav) override (mirrors shells/Shell.js and design/*'s pattern) that renders a real 960x600 headless screenshot of each of the 8 shells (public/imagine/blogx/shots/<slug>.jpg) instead of the default icon+one-line card; the framework's own preview_card() drops the description text once a thumb is passed, so nothing was hand-edited there. NUMBERS at 3440: width used 100%->100% (unchanged, blogx already uses `fill` and reaches the column edge - the site-wide 1856px dead band from round 1 does not apply here, it was already fixed), dead space 0px->0px (unchanged), page height (column body, not document.scrollHeight, which is clamped) 774px->838px (+64px, +8%). At 1280: width used 100%->100%, dead space 0->0, height 736px->833px (+97px, +13%). Invariants unchanged and passing both before and after: no content at x:0 (page starts at x=432/210 after the site's own rail), no prose past 42em (unchanged, the wall's cards are captions not prose), no framed box on an edge (the wall's cells use an inset box-shadow seam, never a border touching the column edge). VERDICT: kept. The height cost is real but small (under 13%) and the win is the whole point of the page - a stranger can now tell apart a hero+wall front, a shut-rail deck, a nested-columns archive and a 4-up parts-column reader at a glance, which no icon combination could do on a realm whose only variable is what the layout looks like.

PERSISTENCE: none. `grep -rn "store()|localStorage" public/imagine/blogx/` returned nothing - every candidate is a static mock over posts.js, no chip, mode or draft is remembered. baseline() not needed. Checked doc links too (the site-wide known trap): no *.md-extension hrefs anywhere under blogx - clean.

UI-TEST: ui-test skill's drive.mjs, two plans. 1280: clicked the real-still "Magazine front" card -> /imagine/blogx/front/, then a post card -> /imagine/blogx/front/tools/panel-playground/, 8 real thumbs confirmed on the landing wall, zero console errors across all 8 steps. 3440: clicked the "Dynamic rail" card -> /imagine/blogx/dig/, then a post card -> /imagine/blogx/dig/framework/layout-generators/, zero console errors across all 7 steps. Every url cold-loads, matching the readme's own claim.

FIVE SENTENCES (after). what: a lab comparing eight complete blog-front layouts, rendered against the same eight fake posts. use: click a card on the wall - each one is now a real screenshot of that shell, not an icon - then click a post or the floor strip to compare. goal: leave knowing which of the eight shapes to actually build a real blog on. hard: 2/5 - the eight cards now show what they claim before you click, the only thing left to learn is the ranked reasoning in the readme. better: formalize the shell-open click as the paging vocabulary's own `takeover` word instead of the custom app.$pages escape, so this realm and /imagine/paging/ agree on one vocabulary for what a click does - parked for the owner (major surgery, a dozen callers, and it changes nothing visible today).

assign.outcome: **Eight icon cards became eight real screenshots — the landing wall now shows what each layout looks like instead of naming it.** `Blog.js` got one `preview(nav)` override (the shells/design pattern) rendering a real 960x600 still of each of the 8 shells; page height at 3440 cost +64px (+8%) for it, width-used and dead-space were already optimal (blogx fixed the site-wide dead-band in round 1) and all three invariants still pass. The 3-column card was not rebuilt: this front door is already a tile wall, and that shape is disproved for a wall of children by five other reviewers tonight. Checked honestly whether moving between the eight shells uses the paging vocabulary (launch/expand/swap/takeover) — it does not: `Blog.container()` mounts straight into `app.$pages`, skipping the columns row entirely, which is more drastic than `takeover` and was left for the owner to fold into the vocabulary (touches all 8 shells plus Section/Post/Part — a dozen callers). Persistence: none. UI-tested at 1280 and 3440 (wall card -> shell -> post, zero console errors both times).
